I'm working through the grid with divider width 7, mapping each labeled block to its mirrored position on the other side and checking for collisions with existing blocks.

8 stays put since its mirrored target overlaps 9a's original position, and 9a moves to cols0-1 in rows6-7 since that spot is free. Piece 4 stays because its target overlaps 9a's original cells. Now assembling the final 8x15 grid with 7 at cols5-6, 2 at cols10-11, 8 at cols9-10, 4 staying at cols3-4, 9 staying at cols11-12, and 9b moved to cols0-1, plus column7 marked as 3.

I'm tracing each block's row/column position and computing where it should move based on its relative offset, checking whether the target location overlaps with the original block (making it stay) or is free (making it move).

Block 6 moves to cols3,4 rows5-6. So the final layout has 2 at cols1,2, 1 at cols4,5, 8 at cols12,13 in rows0-1, and 6 at cols3,4 in rows5-6.

I'm sketching out three test grids with a mix of movable and blocked blocks—an 11-wide, 12-tall grid where each pair has a block on one side with open space on the other, letting me verify simple leftward and rightward shifts work correctly.

For the second pair, I want to test the blocked case where both blocks occupy the same rows and relative column position, so their target swap spots overlap the original positions and neither can move—plus I'll throw in one extra mover to check that unrelated blocks still shift properly alongside the stuck pair.
